    emit([store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "scratch",
                    "row": {"key": batch_id, "kind": "batch", "created_at": now,
                            "payload": json.dumps(items)}}, "vocab-fetch")])

if phase == "vocab-fetch" and op == "insert":
    # Q1: the extractor is shown the axes this memory ALREADY carries, so it reuses
    # a predicate instead of minting a synonym for it. This read is legal HERE and
    # only here -- the extraction lane is asynchronous; the write hot path stays
    # round-trip free.
    # W4: a second half joined it -- the VALUES those axes hold and the ids of the
    # statements holding them.
    # GH #68: the two halves are two QUESTIONS, so they are two bounded reads
    # instead of one unbounded scan they both fold down afterwards. This one opens
    # the window's page: the most recently asserted open facts, which is where a
    # replacement can land at all.
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "facts",
                    "columns": ["subject", "canonical_subject", "predicate",
                                "canonical_predicate", "valid_from"],
                    "where": {"expired_at": {"is_null": True}},
                    "order_by": [{"col": "valid_from", "dir": "desc"},
                                 {"col": "recorded_at", "dir": "desc"},
                                 {"col": "id", "dir": "desc"}],
                    "limit": WINDOW_SCAN_ROWS}, "window-scan")])

if phase == "window-scan" and op == "select":
    axes = candidate_axes(rows_of(d))
    # Nothing open anywhere: no window, and the leg goes straight to the hint. A
    # missing window row is a legal state downstream (the inline ingress has none
    # either) and means exactly what it says -- this batch closes nothing.
    emit([window_read(axes)] if axes else [vocab_read()])

if phase == "window-page" and op == "select":
    rows = rows_of(d)
    # The page is capped and the store returned it axis-major, so a FULL page has
    # exactly one axis that may continue past it: the last one. Its statement count
    # is unproven, so it is dropped instead of counted (rule 2 above).
    incomplete = None
    if rows and len(rows) >= WINDOW_MAX_ROWS:
        incomplete = (str(subject_key(rows[-1]) or ""), str(axis_key(rows[-1]) or ""))
    pool = open_statements(rows, incomplete)
    ops = []
    if pool:
        # GH #67: the POOL, not the window. Which of these axes the extractor is
        # SHOWN is decided at the prompt phase, where the turns are -- and it is
        # the SHOWN one that is parked as `window`, because guard rail 3 checks a
        # `replaces` against what was rendered and never against what was fetched.
        #
        # Parked BEFORE the vocabulary read, because the chain hangs on the
        # vocabulary reply: by the time the meeting-point select is emitted, this
        # row is already behind it in the store's mailbox.
        ops.append(store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "scratch",
                             "row": {"key": batch_id, "kind": "window-pool", "created_at": now,
                                     "payload": json.dumps(pool, sort_keys=True)}},
                            "parked"))
    ops.append(vocab_read())
    emit(ops)

if phase == "vocab" and op == "select":
    emit([store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "scratch",
                    "row": {"key": batch_id, "kind": "vocab", "created_at": now,
                            "payload": json.dumps(known_axes(rows_of(d)))}},
                   "prompt-fetch")])

if phase == "prompt-fetch" and op == "insert":
    # Both sets meet in ONE select: the store has no joins and a stateless cell can
    # hold only one result set at a time (the same trick as the apply phase).
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "scratch",
                    "columns": ["key", "kind", "payload"],
                    "where": {"key": batch_id}}, "prompt")])

if phase == "prompt" and op == "select":
    items, vocab, pool = None, {}, []
    for r in rows_of(d):
        try:
            if r.get("kind") == "batch":
                items = json.loads(r.get("payload") or "[]")
            elif r.get("kind") == "vocab":
                vocab = json.loads(r.get("payload") or "{}")
            elif r.get("kind") == "window-pool":
                # W4: absent is a legal state (the inline ingress has no window,
                # and neither has a batch from before this package). No pool, no
                # window, no replacement offer -- never a park: a missing WINDOW
                # costs a closure, a missing BATCH would cost the turns.
                pool = json.loads(r.get("payload") or "[]")
        except Exception:
            continue
    if items is None:
        # The meeting point did not come back complete. PARK, never close: the
        # rows stay 'claimed' and the flush_reclaim path can hand them back to
        # the queue -- closing here would drop turns that are still on disk.
        park()
    if not items:
        # Nothing to extract: close the batch instead of prompting an empty call.
        emit([store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "pending_extraction",
                        "set": {"status": "done"}, "where": {"batch_id": batch_id}}, "closed")])
    # GH #67: the turns are HERE and nowhere earlier in the chain, so this is the
    # only phase that can ask which of the fetched axes this batch is about.
    window = select_window(pool, items)
    ops = []
    if window:
        # The window as RENDERED, parked under the batch key: guard rail 3 reads
        # this row back in the apply phase, so what the extractor was shown is
        # exactly what it may close. It travels next to the prompt rather than
        # before it because the prompt takes the long way round through a model
        # while this op goes straight to the store -- the row is in place long
        # before any answer comes back.
        ops.append(store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "scratch",
                             "row": {"key": batch_id, "kind": "window", "created_at": now,
                                     "payload": json.dumps(window, sort_keys=True)}},
                            "parked"))
    ops.append({"header": {"route": "extract", "phase": "extract", "batch_id": batch_id},
                "system": {"instructions": {"text": build_instructions(vocab, window)}},
                "messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text", "text": json.dumps(items)}]})
    emit(ops)

# --------------------------------------------------------- extractor output
if phase == "parse":
    if hop.get("finish_reason") == "error":
        # GH #143: a provider error is not a free retry. Read what this batch has
        # already cost before deciding -- the counter lives on the rows, so it
        # survives the requeue that resets their batch_id.
        emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "pending_extraction",
                        "columns": ["id", "attempts"],
                        "where": {"batch_id": batch_id}}, "error-eval")])
    payload = parse_llm_json(first_text(d))
    if payload is None:
        # NOT a requeue: an unparseable answer would come back unparseable and
        # the lane would spin forever. Close the batch and park the raw answer in
        # scratch so it stays auditable and re-processable.
        sys.stderr.write("extract-glue: extractor payload unparseable, batch closed + parked\n")
        emit([store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "scratch",
                        "row": {"key": batch_id, "kind": "extract_failed", "created_at": now,
                                "payload": json.dumps({"raw": first_text(d)[:4000]})}},
                       "parked", batch_id),
              store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "pending_extraction",
                        "set": {"status": "done"}, "where": {"batch_id": batch_id}}, "closed")])
    facts, entities, edges, dropped = validate(payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}, "")
    if dropped:
        sys.stderr.write("extract-glue: dropped %d malformed extractor items\n" % dropped)
    if not facts and not entities:
        emit([store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "pending_extraction",
                        "set": {"status": "done"}, "where": {"batch_id": batch_id}}, "closed")])
    emit([stage_payload(batch_id, facts, entities, edges)])

# GH #143: one provider error later. Either the batch gets another attempt
# behind a growing backoff window, or its budget is used up and it is parked --
# loudly, with the reason on stderr and a mark in `scratch`, because a queue row
# that silently stops moving is the failure mode this whole path exists to
# remove. Nothing is deleted either way: the turns stay on the queue and an
# operator can re-open them by hand.
if phase == "error-eval" and op == "select":
    rows = rows_of(d)
    if not rows:
        park()
    attempt = max(int(r.get("attempts", 0) or 0) for r in rows) + 1
    if attempt >= ERROR_BUDGET:
        sys.stderr.write(
            "extract-glue: batch %s parked after %d consecutive provider errors "
            "(%d rows); no further automatic retry\n" % (batch_id, attempt, len(rows)))
        emit([store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "scratch",
                        "row": {"key": batch_id, "kind": "extract_error_parked",
                                "created_at": now,
                                "payload": json.dumps({"attempts": attempt,
                                                       "rows": len(rows)})}},
                       "parked", batch_id),
              store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "pending_extraction",
                        "set": {"status": "error_parked", "batch_id": "",
                                "attempts": attempt},
                        "where": {"batch_id": batch_id}}, "parked")])
    nb = backoff_until(attempt)
    sys.stderr.write("extract-glue: batch %s failed (attempt %d/%d), retry not before %s\n"
                     % (batch_id, attempt, ERROR_BUDGET, nb))
    emit([store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "pending_extraction",
                    "set": {"status": "pending", "batch_id": "", "attempts": attempt,
                            "not_before": nb},
                    "where": {"batch_id": batch_id}}, "requeue")])

# ------------------------------------------------------------ inline ingress
if phase == "inline":
    # Fail-closed BEFORE the block is read (#244): this ingress mints facts
    # directly, so a payload without provenance is the one path on which an
    # untagged row could reach the store without an episode refusing it first.
    # Terminal and write-free -- the turn stays `pending` and the batched lane
    # picks it up, which is a delay rather than a defect.
    if not audience_ctx:
        sys.stderr.write("extract-glue: inline payload without an audience, dropped\n")
        inline_reject("inline payload rejected: context.audience_set is missing, empty, "
                      "or not a non-empty JSON list of participants -- who was present "
                      "is the gate on every later read and cannot be inferred afterwards",
                      "missing_audience")
    if not channel_ctx:
        sys.stderr.write("extract-glue: inline payload without a channel, dropped\n")
        inline_reject("inline payload rejected: context.channel is missing -- the room is "
                      "recorded explicitly and never parsed out of the session_id prefix",
                      "missing_channel")
    raw = inline_payload_text(d)
    try:
        payload = json.loads(raw)
    except Exception:
        sys.stderr.write("extract-glue: inline payload not JSON, dropped\n")
        inline_reject("inline payload rejected: not JSON")
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        payload = {}
    facts, entities, edges, dropped = validate(payload, payload.get("episode_id", ""))
    # W10b: whatever else happens to this block, it enters the store as a
    # CANDIDATE -- key-shaped predicate, nothing closed on arrival.
    facts = [dict(inline_candidate(f), channel=channel_ctx,
                  audience_set=audience_ctx_text) for f in facts]
    edges = [dict(e, channel=channel_ctx, audience_set=audience_ctx_text) for e in edges]
    # GH #52: the turns this block spoke for leave the queue, whatever becomes of
    # the facts below. The op is emitted NEXT TO the fact lane, never instead of
    # it -- coverage is bookkeeping about turns, the payload is the memory.
    ids = covered_episodes(payload, facts)
    if not ids and session_ctx:
        # THE TOOL FORM (W10b). A block that names no turn and arrives with the
        # session it was written in is a `remember` call. It CANNOT name one: an
        # `episodes.id` is a uuid the hive's writer mints and no front model has
        # ever seen it, so an id a model invented would cover nothing at best and
        # the wrong turn at worst. The hive resolves it instead -- park the block,
        # ask which turn this session is answering, hang the facts on that row.
        # Three hops, on a lane the turn is not waiting for.
        if not facts and not entities:
            sys.stderr.write("extract-glue: inline payload had no valid item, dropped\n")
            inline_reject("inline payload rejected: no valid item (dropped %d)" % dropped)
        bid = "inline:" + str(uuid.uuid4())
        emit([store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "scratch",
                        "row": {"key": bid, "kind": "inline", "created_at": now,
                                "payload": json.dumps({"facts": facts, "entities": entities,
                                                       "edges": edges})}},
                       "inline-turn", bid)])
    ops = [cover_op(ids)] if ids else []
    if not facts and not entities:
        # An EMPTY facts list is a VERDICT, not an absence: the front model read
        # the turn and found nothing memorable. There is nothing to insert, so the
        # block still leaves through the reject port -- but the turn it judged is
        # covered, or the batch buys a second opinion on a question already
        # answered. A payload that named no episode covers nothing and lands here
        # exactly as it did before this package.
        sys.stderr.write("extract-glue: inline payload had no valid item, dropped\n")
        emit(ops + [{"header": {"route": "reject", "phase": "inline", "batch_id": "",
                                "reject_reason": "inline_invalid"},
                     "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "x-reject",
                                   "text": "inline payload rejected: no valid item (dropped %d)"
                                           % dropped}]}])
    emit(ops + [stage_payload("inline:" + str(uuid.uuid4()), facts, entities, edges)])

# ---------------------------------------------------- inline bind (W10b)
if phase == "inline-turn" and op == "insert":
    emit([bind_read()])

if phase == "inline-bind" and op == "select":
    rows = rows_of(d)
    if not rows:
        # Nothing to bind to: the per-turn lane is off, or the episode has not
        # landed yet. Cover NOTHING and stage nothing -- see `inline_reject`.
        sys.stderr.write("extract-glue: inline block has no turn to bind to, dropped\n")
        inline_reject("inline payload rejected: no episode for this session")
    ep = rows[0]
    # The resolved id rides in the batch key, the way the collector's prune lane
    # carries its own second value: the meeting point below answers with the
    # parked block and nothing else, and a stateless cell holds one result set at
    # a time. The pure key is restored on the other side, so everything
    # downstream sees the ordinary batch id it always saw.
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "scratch",
                    "columns": ["key", "kind", "payload"],
                    "where": {"key": batch_id}},
                   "inline-apply", batch_id + "|" + str(ep.get("id") or ""))])

if phase == "inline-apply" and op == "select":
    bid, _, episode_id = batch_id.partition("|")
    block = None
    for r in rows_of(d):
        if r.get("kind") == "inline":
            block = r
    if block is None or not episode_id:
        sys.stderr.write("extract-glue: inline block lost between park and bind, dropped\n")
        inline_reject("inline payload rejected: parked block not found")
    try:
        parked_block = json.loads(block.get("payload") or "{}")
    except Exception:
        sys.stderr.write("extract-glue: parked inline block unreadable, dropped\n")
        inline_reject("inline payload rejected: parked block unreadable")
    facts = [inline_candidate(f, episode_id)
             for f in parked_block.get("facts", []) or []]
    entities = parked_block.get("entities", []) or []
    edges = [dict(e, episode_id=episode_id)
             for e in parked_block.get("edges", []) or []]
    # Coverage (GitHub #52) and the fact lane leave together, exactly as they do
    # on the form that names its own turn: coverage is bookkeeping about a turn,
    # the payload is the memory, and neither replaces the other.
    emit([cover_op([episode_id]), stage_payload(bid, facts, entities, edges)])

# --------------------------------------------------------- dedup + apply
if phase == "dedup" and op == "insert":
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "facts",
                    "columns": ["episode_id", "claim_hash"], "where": {}}, "known")])

if phase == "known" and op == "select":
    known = sorted({str(r.get("episode_id", "")) + ":" + str(r.get("claim_hash", ""))
                    for r in rows_of(d)})
    row = {"key": batch_id, "kind": "known", "created_at": now, "payload": json.dumps(known)}
    # SEQUENTIAL, not parallel: two selects fanned out from here would both land
    # in scratch and both trigger the merge, and apply would run twice (measured:
    # duplicate facts). One chain, one apply.
    emit([store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "scratch", "row": row}, "eps-fetch")])

if phase == "eps-fetch" and op == "insert":
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "episodes",
                    "columns": ["id", "happened_at", "session_id", "channel",
                                "audience_set"], "where": {}},
                   "known-eps")])

if phase == "known-eps" and op == "select":
    # event times of the episodes this batch refers to — the third set of the
    # join-less meeting point in `scratch`
    # Since W1 the session travels with the instant: the fact row carries the
    # origin of its turn, so the chain rule can ask whether two values were
    # stated in ONE conversation or in two (statement identity #13, ruling Q3),
    # and this select is the only place in the lane that knows.
    # #244: and the AUDIENCE travels with the session, for the same reason and
    # one question further on. A fact is only ever as tellable as the turn it was
    # learned in, so the participant set and the room of the episode are what the
    # fact row copies -- never the round that happens to be extracting it.
    eps = {str(r.get("id")): {"happened_at": r.get("happened_at"),
                             "session_id": r.get("session_id"),
                             "channel": r.get("channel"),
                             "audience_set": r.get("audience_set")}
           for r in rows_of(d) if r.get("id")}
    row = {"key": batch_id, "kind": "episodes", "created_at": now, "payload": json.dumps(eps)}
    emit([store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "scratch", "row": row}, "merge")])

if phase == "merge" and op == "insert":
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "scratch",
                    "columns": ["key", "kind", "payload"],
                    "where": {"key": batch_id}}, "apply")])

if phase == "apply" and op == "select":
    payload_row, known_row, eps_row, window_row = None, None, None, None
    for r in rows_of(d):
        if r.get("kind") == "payload":
            payload_row = r
        elif r.get("kind") == "known":
            known_row = r
        elif r.get("kind") == "episodes":
            eps_row = r
        elif r.get("kind") == "window":
            window_row = r
    if payload_row is None or known_row is None or eps_row is None:
        park()
    try:
        staged = json.loads(payload_row.get("payload") or "{}")
        known = set(json.loads(known_row.get("payload") or "[]"))
        episode_time = json.loads(eps_row.get("payload") or "{}")
    except Exception:
        park()
    # W4, ruling Q2 guard rail 3: the PROOF of what the extractor was shown, read
    # back from the row the vocabulary phase parked. Not optional and not a
    # comment -- a `replaces` naming anything outside this map is discarded, so a
    # missing window (the inline ingress, a batch from before this package) means
    # no closure at all rather than an unguarded one. The axis travels with the
    # id because the closure ECHOES it in its `where`, exactly as the judge's does.
    # GH #71: and the INSTANT travels with it too, because the second guard is a
    # comparison and this is the only place that holds both sides of it. A window
    # row parked by the previous version has no `last_asserted`, so `since` is the
    # fallback -- on a statement asserted once the two are the same value, which is
    # the shape of nearly every entry.
    seen = {}
    try:
        for a in json.loads(window_row.get("payload") or "[]") if window_row else []:
            for s in a.get("statements") or []:
                if s.get("id"):
                    seen[str(s["id"])] = (str(a.get("subject") or ""),
                                          str(a.get("predicate") or ""),
                                          str(s.get("claim") or ""),
                                          str(s.get("last_asserted")
                                              or s.get("since") or ""))
    except Exception:
        seen = {}
    out = []
    written = 0
    embed_items = []
    closures, refusals, unseen = [], [], 0
    for f in staged.get("facts", []):
        key = str(f.get("episode_id", "")) + ":" + str(f.get("claim_hash", ""))
        if key in known:
            continue
        known.add(key)
        # The episode this fact hangs on, as the scratch row carries it. The dict
        # shape is W1's; a payload staged by the previous version holds the bare
        # instant, and a crash between staging and apply must not cost the event
        # time that payload already had.
        ep = episode_time.get(str(f.get("episode_id"))) or {}
        if not isinstance(ep, dict):
            ep = {"happened_at": ep}
        # EVENT time, in this order: what the extractor claimed > when the episode
        # actually happened > our clock. The middle step is the one that was
        # missing; without it every fact is stamped with the ingest instant.
        valid_from = f.get("valid_from") or ep.get("happened_at") or now
        row = {"id": str(uuid.uuid4()), "episode_id": f.get("episode_id"),
               "session_id": ep.get("session_id") or "",
               # #244: inherited from the episode, exactly the way session_id is.
               # The fallback is the provenance the INLINE ingress carried in on
               # its own context, for the one case the episode row cannot answer
               # (it is not in the page above); an empty value is left empty,
               # because an untagged row is invisible and a guessed one is a leak.
               "channel": ep.get("channel") or f.get("channel") or "",
               "audience_set": ep.get("audience_set") or f.get("audience_set") or "",
               "subject": f.get("subject"), "predicate": f.get("predicate"),
               "claim": f.get("claim"), "claim_hash": f.get("claim_hash"),
               "fact_kind": f.get("fact_kind"), "valid_from": valid_from,
               "valid_until": f.get("valid_until"), "recorded_at": now,
               "expired_at": None, "superseded_by": None, "confidence": f.get("confidence")}
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "facts", "row": row}, "applied"))
        emb_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        # The queued row is written FIRST and unconditionally: the NULL queue is
        # the durable part, the embed call is the optional part.
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "embeddings",
                             "row": {"id": emb_id, "owner_table": "facts",
                                     "owner_id": row["id"], "model_id": "", "dim": 0,
                                     "binarization_version": "", "blob": None,
                                     "status": "queued", "created_at": now}}, "applied"))
        embed_items.append({"embedding_id": emb_id, "text": f.get("claim")})
        written += 1
        # W4: the closure this fact asked for. Emitted AFTER its own insert, so
        # `superseded_by` names a row that exists, and in the W3 write form down
        # to the column -- the read path cannot tell the two producers apart and
        # must not be able to.
        target = str(f.get("replaces") or "")
        if not target or target == row["id"]:
            continue
        if target not in seen:
            unseen += 1
            continue
        subject, predicate, old_claim, held_until = seen[target]
        # GH #71: DIRECTION. The window says WHICH statements may be closed; it
        # never said which of the two is newer, and one of the first three live
        # extractor closures ended a statement three days its senior -- the gold
        # answer, ended by a fact from before it was ever said. A replacement is a
        # claim about time, so the lane checks the time.
        #
        # The comparison is the recency this lane already sorts by,
        # (valid_from, recorded_at, id), and two of its three components are
        # decided before it is evaluated:
        #   * recorded_at -- the statement being closed was read out of the store
        #     by THIS batch, so it was recorded before this batch's clock. A tie on
        #     valid_from is therefore resolved in favour of the new fact, which is
        #     what keeps two turns of ONE session updating a value.
        #   * id -- a uuid4 carries no time. It makes a sort deterministic and it
        #     never decides a direction.
        # What is left is valid_from, on the assertion still standing: the row the
        # closure names, and the row whose own instant a reader compares afterwards.
        #
        # A refusal is NOT an error and not a dropped fact: the mint above already
        # happened, only the closure falls away, both statements stay open and the
        # nightly round gets to judge the pair with the whole axis in front of it.
        if held_until and valid_from and held_until > valid_from:
            refusals.append({"id": target, "superseded_by": row["id"],
                             "subject": subject, "predicate": predicate,
                             "replaced_claim": old_claim, "claim": row["claim"],
                             "episode_id": row["episode_id"],
                             "held_until": held_until, "valid_from": valid_from,
                             "reason": "the replacing fact starts at " + valid_from
                                       + ", before the " + held_until
                                       + " this statement was last asserted at"})
            continue
        closures.append({"id": target, "superseded_by": row["id"],
                         "expired_at": valid_from, "subject": subject,
                         "predicate": predicate, "replaced_claim": old_claim,
                         "claim": row["claim"], "episode_id": row["episode_id"]})
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "facts",
                             "set": {"expired_at": valid_from,
                                     "superseded_by": row["id"],
                                     "closure_source": CLOSURE_SOURCE},
                             "where": {"id": target, "canonical_subject": subject,
                                       "canonical_predicate": predicate,
                                       "expired_at": {"is_null": True}}}, "applied"))
    if unseen:
        # Loud, because this is the guard rail firing: either the model invented a
        # reference or the window it was shown does not match the store any more.
        sys.stderr.write("extract-glue: dropped %d replaces outside the extraction window\n"
                         % unseen)
    if closures:
        # The reasons, parked under the batch key -- the extraction lane's
        # equivalent of the run receipt the night folds its closures into. The
        # attribution points HERE, so a closed fact reads back to the turn that
        # replaced it and one batch is reverted with one `where`.
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "scratch",
                             "row": {"key": batch_id, "kind": "extract-closures",
                                     "created_at": now,
                                     "payload": json.dumps(closures, sort_keys=True)}},
                            "parked"))
    if refusals:
        # GH #71: and the closures this batch did NOT write, in the same currency
        # and under the same key. A guard whose refusals are invisible is how the
        # direction defect survived a whole track: `closures_by_extract` was the
        # only counter, and a silent drop moves no counter at all. The row names
        # both values and both instants, so a refusal can be read back exactly the
        # way a closure can -- and one query says how often the guard fired.
        sys.stderr.write("extract-glue: refused %d replaces on direction "
                         "(the statement is newer than the fact replacing it)\n"
                         % len(refusals))
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "scratch",
                             "row": {"key": batch_id, "kind": "extract-refusals",
                                     "created_at": now,
                                     "payload": json.dumps(refusals, sort_keys=True)}},
                            "parked"))
    for e in staged.get("entities", []):
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "entities",
                             "row": {"id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
                                     "canonical_name": e.get("canonical_name"),
                                     "kind": e.get("kind"), "aliases": e.get("aliases")}},
                            "applied"))
    for e in staged.get("edges", []):
        # #244: an edge is the graph leg of tier 1 and leaves the read path on its
        # own, so it is tagged on its own -- from the episode it names, the same
        # inheritance the fact above makes.
        eep = episode_time.get(str(e.get("episode_id"))) or {}
        if not isinstance(eep, dict):
            eep = {}
        out.append(store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "entity_edges",
                             "row": {"id": str(uuid.uuid4()), "src_entity": e.get("src_entity"),
                                     "dst_entity": e.get("dst_entity"),
                                     "edge_kind": e.get("edge_kind"), "weight": e.get("weight"),
                                     "episode_id": e.get("episode_id"),
                                     "channel": eep.get("channel") or e.get("channel") or "",
                                     "audience_set": eep.get("audience_set")
                                                     or e.get("audience_set") or "",
                                     "valid_from": now, "valid_until": None}}, "applied"))
    out.append(store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "pending_extraction",
                         "set": {"status": "done"}, "where": {"batch_id": batch_id}}, "closed"))
    if embed_items:
        out.append({"header": {"route": "embed", "phase": "embed", "batch_id": batch_id},
                    "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "x-embed",
                                  "text": json.dumps({"items": embed_items})}]})
    emit(out)

park()

batch_tokens.description: Accumulated token estimate that opens the extraction gate (MEMORY_BATCH_TOKENS). A RECOMMENDED default, not a mandate (GH #51): the gate exists so that one model call serves many turns, and the value decides how much freshness that costs. 128 keeps a fact queryable roughly a turn or two after the message that carried it

batch_max_age_min.description: Age of the oldest queued item that opens the gate regardless of size (MEMORY_BATCH_MAX_AGE_MIN). Also a RECOMMENDED default (GH #51): it bounds the worst case, so a short message followed by silence waits about two minutes for its fact rather than half an hour. Raise it only if model cost outranks freshness for this colony

batch_claim_lease_min.description: How long a claimed batch is held before a recovery sweep (mem_phase='flush' with flush_reclaim='1') may hand its rows back to the queue (MEMORY_BATCH_CLAIM_LEASE_MIN, GH #72). Must exceed one full extraction cycle -- the extractor's message_timeout is 180 s, so anything below about 4 minutes reclaims batches that are still in flight and pays for them twice

extract_error_budget.description: Consecutive provider errors one batch may cost before the lane parks it instead of re-sending (MEMORY_EXTRACT_ERROR_BUDGET, GH #143). Parked is terminal for the automatic lane -- the rows keep their turns, carry status 'error_parked' and a mark in `scratch`, and a recovery sweep does not take them back: whatever failed three times in a row will fail the fourth, and a queue that re-sends it forever is a colony that looks idle while it spends

extract_backoff_sec.description: Base of the backoff window after a failed extraction attempt (MEMORY_EXTRACT_BACKOFF_SEC, GH #143); it doubles per attempt, so 60 gives 60 s / 120 s / 240 s. Without it the flush cadence IS the retry cadence -- measured 107 of 111 extraction responses were retries of one failing batch inside nine minutes

extract_window_axes.description: Axes whose OPEN statements travel in the extraction prompt as the replacement window (MEMORY_EXTRACT_WINDOW_AXES, statement identity W4). An axis with more open statements than one page is skipped rather than truncated, and the ranking is recency

extract_vocab_rows.description: Cap of the axis-hint read (MEMORY_EXTRACT_VOCAB_ROWS, GH #68). The read is deduplicated by the store, so this counts AXES (one row per written spelling of a subject/predicate pair), not facts. Ordering is subject-major, so the cap cuts whole subjects off the tail

extract_window_scan.description: Cap of the recency page that picks the window's candidate axes (MEMORY_EXTRACT_WINDOW_SCAN, GH #68). Counts open fact rows, most recently asserted first; an axis whose newest assertion falls outside this page is not offered for replacement in this batch

extract_window_rows.description: Cap of the window's own page, which reads the candidate axes whole (MEMORY_EXTRACT_WINDOW_ROWS, GH #68). Ordering is axis-major, so a page that comes back full has exactly one axis it cannot prove complete: the last, which is dropped rather than counted

description.purpose: The extraction lane's state machine: accumulates queued turns, opens the batch gate at ~128 tokens or a 2-minute-old item, claims the batch with an atomic guarded update, reads the identity axes this memory already carries (the canonical columns, so a merge the nightly GC judged is what the extractor sees) and the open statements of the axes it touched most recently, each through a read with a stated ordering and a bound of its own, cuts that pool down to the axes the batch's own turns are ABOUT, prompts the extractor with them plus the curated core vocabulary, validates its payload against the bi-temporal fact contract and writes deduped facts/entities/edges plus queued embedding rows. The SAME validator serves the inline ingress.
description.use_when: Behind the writer (queue lane) and behind the front-line llm (inline ingress port, store_origin='inline'). One LLM call per batch, never per message. A message with context.mem_phase='flush' drains the queue immediately, whatever the gate would say. The inline ingress prompts nobody, so ITS contract lives in the front model's persona: the hive ships that block in inline-contract.md and it states the same world-state discipline this lane renders for its own extractor (GH #53).
description.not_in_scope: No consolidation (that is dream-glue), no ranking, no embedding computation (that is the embed lane), no state of its own — every intermediate result lives in the store (DEC-009).
description.emits_meaning: route xstore: the store op of the current phase; hop.phase and hop.batch_id are promoted to context by the edge and are the only state carrier. route extract: the assembled batch for the extractor, together with the extraction contract as system.instructions -- shape, fact_kind semantics, the O-6 discipline (world state only, never conversation metadata, never an echo of an assistant turn) and the P1 canonicalisation rules (predicate keys are English snake_case, the core vocabulary with its single/multi split, the axes already in use per subject, the rule that a predicate names the subject matter and never the speech act -- an intention is `fact_kind: foresight` on the matter's own axis, not a `plans_to_*` axis of its own -- and the entity-fidelity rule that keeps every name byte-faithful). route embed: texts for the embed lane after the facts landed. route reject: an inline payload this lane would not take -- one that did not survive validation (hop.reject_reason 'inline_invalid'), or one whose provenance was incomplete (#244: 'missing_audience' / 'missing_channel'). Best effort, logged, never coupled to the answer path, and always WRITE-FREE: the turn stays `pending` and the batched lane picks it up, because one extraction later is a delay and a fact hung on the wrong audience is a leak.
description.consumes_meaning: context.mem_phase selects the state, hop.operation/hop.rows_affected carry the store's answer: rows_affected>0 on the claim update means this worker owns the batch, 0 means it lost the race and parks. context.store_origin distinguishes the batched lane ('extract') from the inline ingress ('inline') and swallows the raw episode echo ('episode'). pending_extraction.status is the lane's own bookkeeping and names WHO owes a turn its extraction and WHO settled it: 'pending' = nobody has claimed it, 'claimed' = one batch owns it right now, 'done' = the batch that owned it finished, 'inline' = the front model already extracted the turn and no batch is ever offered it (GH #52). Gate, claim guard and flush all read 'pending', which is what makes the inline mark the whole mechanism; flush_reclaim hands 'claimed' back to 'pending' and never touches the other two -- and since GH #72 it only reaches claims whose LEASE has expired (pending_extraction.claimed_at older than MEMORY_BATCH_CLAIM_LEASE_MIN), so a batch whose extractor call is still in flight is left alone instead of being extracted and paid for twice. #244: context.audience_set and context.channel are the INLINE ingress's own gate -- that path mints facts directly, so a block arriving without them is refused on the reject lane instead of writing an untagged row. The batched lane is not gated here: its facts and edges inherit channel and audience_set from the EPISODE they hang on, exactly the way session_id does, and the queue row carries a readable copy the writer put on the queue item. Nothing on this lane ever rewrites a provenance it read (ADR-0002 E12).
examples: queue below 128 tokens and younger than 2 minutes -> select shows the sum -> park, nothing claimed, no LLM call

queue at/over 128 tokens -> update status pending->claimed (rows_affected 3) -> batch parked in scratch -> the vocabulary leg's three bounded reads (recency page of the open facts, the candidate axes read whole, the deduplicated axis hint) -> window and axes parked -> one select reads them back -> batch prompt -> extractor

the store already carries user|favorite_color -> the prompt lists that axis -> a later "my favourite colour is green now" lands on favorite_color instead of opening favourite_colour, and the version chain fires

the store already carries user|personal_record "a personal best of 27:12" and eleven newer axes -> recency alone would push that axis out of the window, so the turn "I want to beat my personal best and run 25:50" is shown it because it is what the turn is ABOUT -> the intention lands on personal_record as foresight instead of opening plans_to_beat (GH #67)

the window shows lives_in "the suburbs", asserted 2023-05-27, and the extracted fact "Chicago" is dated 2023-05-24 -> the `replaces` is REFUSED on direction (GH #71): the fact is minted, both statements stay open for the nightly currency question, and the pair is parked as `extract-refusals` under the batch key

inline {"facts":[{subject,predicate,claim,fact_kind}]} -> validated -> deduped by (episode_id, claim_hash) -> facts row + queued embedding row, and the queue rows of every episode the block named go from 'pending' to 'inline' (GH #52) so no batch is ever offered those turns

inline {"episode_id":"e7","facts":[]} -> nothing to insert, route reject -- and e7 is covered anyway: an empty list is the front model's VERDICT that the turn held nothing memorable, and re-asking a second model would mint the duplicate this mark exists to stop
inline garbage -> route reject + stderr warning, zero store writes, no episode covered (a block that proves nothing about a turn leaves that turn to the batch)
